EDIT TO SAY: After reading over this some more, I have to say OP totally misrepresented the article and the title is total click-bait. There is NO DRM being implemented whatsoever. This sort of thing is routine for device communication, all sorts of protocols have ways of consistently verifying what is on the other end of the connection. Sure it would make old cables obsolete since they would fail the authentication/handshake/what-have-you, but it would also mean that non-certified, potentially non-compliant cables could be rejected if needed. This does not mean that these tech companies can introduce handshakes that only work with their cables/devices, it just means that they would have to get certified for and implement this universally-agreed-upon handshake. It's a pain in the butt now that saves a lot of headache down the road.

Honestly I would prefer if USB C stays as open and unmolested as possible, I've grown quite fond of it and I don't want it getting restricted. USB-C, on the other hand, is a format published by a non-profit organization that Wikipedia tells me is the USB Implementers Forum.
